chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
There is no problem with the Muhrim tying a strip around his head due to headache.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible
key_terms.يُعَصِّبَ: To tie/bind with a cloth or strip

ai.seo_question: Can a person in Ihram tie a cloth around their head for a headache?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that tying a cloth (ta'sib) for medical relief from headache is permissible, distinguishing it from the general prohibition of covering the head for adornment or warmth. This ruling underscores the Shia principle of *darura* (necessity) in Hajj jurisprudence, where the preservation of health overrides the ritual restriction of head covering for men in Ihram.
